title: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional (DOP-C02)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 exam guide (six official domains and weightings). Not a capture of past questions.

items.stem: A development team wants every push to its CodeCommit repository to start a pipeline build immediately instead of waiting for periodic polling. Which configuration delivers near-real-time pipeline starts?
options: A CodePipeline source action that uses CodeCommit with event-based change detection so commits start the pipeline at once
A CloudWatch rule that polls the repository every minute
A CodeBuild project that scans the repository on a cron schedule
A manual pipeline start performed from the console after each commit
items.explanation: CodePipeline supports event-based change detection for CodeCommit, which starts the pipeline as soon as a commit arrives. Polling rules and scheduled builds add latency, and manual starts defeat automation.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A company must deploy a new version of a web application to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances with no downtime and the option to shift traffic gradually to the new version while keeping the old fleet available for rollback. Which CodeDeploy deployment type meets this need?
options: An in-place deployment that replaces instances one at a time
A blue/green deployment that provisions a replacement fleet behind the load balancer
A manual deployment performed by terminating instances
A deployment that stops all instances before installing the new version
items.explanation: Blue/green provisions a replacement fleet and shifts load-balancer traffic only after the new instances pass health checks, so there is no downtime and the old fleet remains for rollback. In-place replacement serves both versions during the change, manual termination is uncontrolled, and stopping all instances causes an outage.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team deploys a Lambda function and needs to release a new version to a small percentage of callers before shifting all traffic, while automatically reverting if the error rate rises. Which mechanism should be used?
options: Deploy the function to a second Region and route all traffic there
Overwrite the published function so every caller receives the new code at once
Publish a new version and use an alias with weighted routing that CodeDeploy shifts over time
Create a second function and let each client choose randomly between them
items.explanation: Lambda aliases support weighted traffic shifting, and CodeDeploy can manage a canary or linear shift that monitors alarms and rolls back on failure. Overwriting the function exposes everyone immediately, and client-side or Region-level routing does not provide controlled rollout or automatic rollback.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A pipeline must stop and require a recorded human decision before a build is released to production. Which CodePipeline action should be added between the staging and production stages?
options: A Lambda action that sleeps for an hour
A build action that always succeeds
An IAM policy that denies the production role
A manual approval action
items.explanation: A manual approval action halts the pipeline until an authorized user approves, giving a controlled and auditable gate before production. A sleep action records no decision, an always-succeeding build gates nothing, and an IAM denial would stop deployments entirely rather than approve them.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A build must compile code, run unit tests, and produce an artifact that downstream stages promote unchanged to every environment. Which CodeBuild and CodePipeline configuration supports this immutable promotion?
options: Have the buildspec output artifacts that CodePipeline passes to later stages
Commit the compiled binary into the repository after every build
Store the binary on one EC2 instance that all stages read from
Rebuild from source in every stage so each environment compiles its own copy
items.explanation: CodeBuild can emit artifacts that CodePipeline carries forward, so one tested binary is promoted to every environment, which supports immutable deployments. Rebuilding per stage can produce a different binary, committing build output bloats the repository, and a single instance is neither durable nor reproducible.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team wants failed unit tests during a CodeBuild run to stop the pipeline immediately rather than allow a broken build to proceed. Which behavior should the buildspec rely on?
options: Ignore the test command exit code so the build continues
Ensure the test command returns a non-zero exit code so the build phase fails
Add a manual approval step after the build
Enable dependency caching for the test packages
items.explanation: CodeBuild marks a build failed when a phase command exits non-zero, which stops the pipeline. Ignoring the exit code hides failures, a manual approval does not evaluate test results, and caching only speeds up repeats.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A company needs a private, versioned repository for internal libraries that its build projects reference, and it wants to avoid hand-managed file shares. Which service should be used?
options: A CodeCommit repository holding the compiled packages
An S3 bucket with public read access
AWS CodeArtifact with a repository and an upstream connection
An EC2 instance serving files over plain FTP
items.explanation: CodeArtifact is a managed artifact repository that stores and versions packages and can proxy public repositories. A public bucket exposes internal libraries, a plain FTP server is unmanaged and insecure, and CodeCommit is intended for source code rather than dependency packages.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A pipeline needs database credentials during a build but must never store them in the repository or the buildspec. Which approach follows best practice?
options: Commit an encrypted file to the repository and publish the key in the readme
Place the credentials in an environment variable committed to source control
Hard-code the credentials inside the buildspec file
Retrieve the credentials from AWS Secrets Manager at run time using the build role
items.explanation: Retrieving secrets from Secrets Manager at run time grants the build role least-privilege access and keeps secrets out of source control. Hard-coded or committed credentials stay exposed, and publishing a decryption key defeats the encryption.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: One pipeline deploys the same application to development, staging, and production accounts. Which design lets the production stage deploy securely without long-lived credentials?
options: Assume a role in the target account using a cross-account trust configured for that stage
Give every developer the production account root credentials
Disable authentication for the production deployment stage
Copy long-lived IAM user keys for the production account into the pipeline
items.explanation: Cross-account roles let each stage assume short-lived credentials in the target account, which avoids static keys and supports least privilege. Copying long-lived keys is insecure and hard to rotate, sharing root credentials violates least privilege, and disabling authentication removes control.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team running Elastic Beanstalk wants a deployment that launches a complete new set of instances and swaps them into service only after they pass health checks, without reducing capacity during the update. Which deployment policy should it choose?
options: All at once
Immutable
Rolling
Rolling with additional batch
items.explanation: Immutable deployment launches a full new set of instances in a temporary Auto Scaling group and swaps them in only when healthy. All at once causes downtime, rolling reduces capacity during the update, and rolling with additional batch still modifies the existing instance set in place.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A company wants to release a new web version by switching DNS so users move to a separate new environment and can be moved back quickly if problems appear. Which blue/green approach should be used?
options: Increasing the instance size in the existing environment
Moving an Elastic IP address between two environments
Two identical environments switched with Route 53 weighted or failover records
Updating one environment in place during business hours
items.explanation: Blue/green with DNS switches weighted or failover records to move traffic between two identical environments and allows a quick rollback. In-place updates serve both versions from one environment, a larger instance does not separate versions, and moving an Elastic IP is not a DNS-based traffic switch.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team wants CodeDeploy to revert automatically when a CloudWatch alarm fires shortly after a production deployment. Which configuration should be added to the deployment group?
options: Instruct operators to watch a dashboard and roll back by hand
Add a second manual approval before the rollout
Increase the deployment timeout to several hours
Enable automatic rollback and associate the CloudWatch alarm with the deployment
items.explanation: CodeDeploy can monitor CloudWatch alarms during a deployment and automatically roll back to the last known good revision when one fires. Manual watching is slow, another approval only delays the release, and a longer timeout does not detect or correct a bad deployment.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A company wants integration tests to run against a freshly configured environment and then have that environment removed automatically as part of the pipeline. Which approach should be used?
options: Have a pipeline stage provision a temporary environment, run the tests, and tear it down
Keep one static shared test environment that everyone uses indefinitely
Skip integration testing whenever the change set is small
Test only in production after users report defects
items.explanation: Ephemeral test environments created and destroyed by the pipeline give clean, isolated integration testing and then free resources. Testing only in production exposes users, a permanent shared environment drifts and collides, and skipping tests raises release risk.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team discovers that the artifact running in production differs from the one that passed testing because a later pipeline stage recompiled the code. Which practice prevents this discrepancy?
options: Deploy from a developer workstation to shorten the cycle
Promote the exact artifact built once through every stage
Rebuild from source in each stage to save storage
Allow each stage to modify the artifact for its environment
items.explanation: Building once and promoting the identical artifact guarantees that production runs exactly what was tested. Rebuilding can introduce differences, mutating the artifact invalidates the test result, and deploying from a workstation bypasses the controlled pipeline.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team manages a serverless application with the AWS Serverless Application Model and wants safe deployment of new Lambda versions with gradual traffic shifting and automatic rollback. Which SAM feature should be used?
options: Publishing the function under a new name for each deployment
An API Gateway stage variable pinned to one fixed version
Deployment preferences that use CodeDeploy to shift traffic and roll back on alarms
Overwriting the production function in place on every release
items.explanation: SAM integrates with CodeDeploy so serverless deployments can use canary or linear traffic shifting and automatic rollback on alarms. In-place overwrites give no gradual shift, renaming functions breaks integrations, and a fixed stage variable does not shift traffic over time.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A regulated team wants pull requests against a protected branch to require approval from at least two named reviewers before they can be merged. Which CodeCommit feature enforces this?
options: A note in the team wiki requesting two approvals
A CloudWatch alarm that fires when a pull request is merged
A Lambda function that emails the reviewers after a merge
An approval rule template attached to the repository
items.explanation: CodeCommit approval rule templates require a set number of approvals from specified users before a pull request can merge. Documentation and email rely on goodwill, and a post-merge alarm is too late to prevent an unapproved change.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.stem: A team running a canary deployment wants the release to revert automatically when the new version degrades the user experience. Which signals should drive the deployment alarms?
options: Service CloudWatch metrics such as error rate and latency
The number of commits merged before the release
The total size of the deployment artifact
Only the CPU utilization of the build server
items.explanation: Deployment alarms should track service-level signals such as error rate and latency so a canary that degrades triggers rollback. Build-server CPU, commit counts, and artifact size do not reflect user-facing health.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - SDLC Automation

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A company must deploy a baseline of IAM roles and AWS Config rules into every account of its organization, including accounts created later. Which CloudFormation feature should it use?
options: A single stack deployed once in the management account
CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions and automatic deployment
A shell script that a person runs in each account
A nested stack in one account that imports the other accounts
items.explanation: StackSets create, update, and delete stacks across many accounts and Regions, and service-managed permissions with automatic deployment cover new accounts. A single stack affects one account, manual scripts are not automatic, and nested stacks stay within one account and Region.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A team suspects that manual changes have altered production resources that CloudFormation created. Which CloudFormation capability detects the difference between the template and the actual resources?
options: Stack policies
Change sets
Drift detection
Rollback triggers
items.explanation: Drift detection compares the actual resource configuration with the template and reports differences, revealing out-of-band changes. Change sets preview a planned update, rollback triggers react to alarms during an update, and stack policies protect resources during updates.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: Before updating a production stack, a team wants to review exactly which resources CloudFormation will add, modify, or replace. Which feature provides this preview?
options: A stack policy that denies all updates
A snapshot taken after the update is applied
A drift detection run on the stack
A change set created before the update
items.explanation: A change set summarizes the operations an update will perform, including resource replacement, before the change is executed. A stack policy can protect resources but does not preview changes, snapshots are taken after the fact, and drift detection reports current differences rather than a planned update.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A team wants to reuse a standard networking template inside several application templates without copying the resource definitions into each one. Which CloudFormation construct should be used?
options: A nested stack referenced from the parent template
Copying the networking resources into every template
A change set shared between templates
An output value typed into each template by hand
items.explanation: Nested stacks let a parent template reference a child template so common resources are defined once and reused. Copying duplicates maintenance, change sets apply to one stack, and manually typed outputs invite drift and errors.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A team needs CloudFormation to create a resource type that it does not support natively, using custom provisioning logic written in a Lambda function. Which mechanism should be used?
options: A parameter with an allowed value list
A custom resource backed by the Lambda function
An output that returns a fixed string
A mapping declared in the template
items.explanation: Custom resources invoke a Lambda function to create, update, and delete resources that CloudFormation does not support natively. Outputs, mappings, and parameters only pass values and cannot provision custom resources.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A developer wants to define AWS infrastructure with familiar programming constructs and have the tool generate CloudFormation templates. Which tool should be used?
options: A spreadsheet listing resource names
Manual resource creation in the AWS Management Console
The AWS Cloud Development Kit
The CloudFormation visual designer alone
items.explanation: The AWS Cloud Development Kit lets developers define infrastructure with programming constructs and synthesizes CloudFormation templates for deployment. The visual designer has no programming model, and spreadsheets or console work are not repeatable infrastructure as code.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A company wants to build hardened Amazon Machine Images on a schedule through a documented workflow that applies patches and then tests the result. Which service should be used?
options: Manually created instances captured as AMIs each month
AWS Elastic Beanstalk building images during deployment
AWS Batch running a shell script on one instance
EC2 Image Builder with a pipeline that builds and tests images
items.explanation: EC2 Image Builder defines image recipes and pipelines that build, test, and distribute AMIs automatically. Manual captures are error-prone and undocumented, AWS Batch is a compute service, and Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications rather than producing golden AMIs.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A company wants to apply and continuously re-enforce a baseline configuration such as an agent install and registry settings across a fleet of managed instances. Which AWS Systems Manager capability should be used?
options: State Manager associations that apply the configuration on a schedule
A one-time manual login to each instance
A CodeCommit repository of configuration notes
An Auto Scaling group launch template alone
items.explanation: State Manager associations define and reapply a desired state across a managed fleet so configuration stays consistent. Manual logins do not scale, notes enforce nothing, and a launch template only affects newly launched instances and not drift on running ones.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A company must patch a fleet of Windows and Linux instances on a defined schedule with controlled reboots and compliance reporting. Which Systems Manager capability should be used?
options: A CloudFormation stack that restarts instances weekly
Patch Manager with a patch baseline and a maintenance window
Amazon Inspector installing patches automatically
Turning on automatic updates inside each application
items.explanation: Patch Manager uses a patch baseline to select approved patches and a maintenance window to apply them with controlled reboots and reporting. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities but does not install patches, application-level updates miss the operating system, and restarting instances does not patch them.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: An application reads configuration values such as feature flags and database host names at startup and needs them stored centrally with versioning and optional encryption. Which service should be used?
options: An S3 bucket without encryption or versioning
Environment variables compiled into the application
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
A text file copied onto each instance at launch
items.explanation: Parameter Store centralizes configuration with versioning and supports encrypted SecureString values that applications read at run time. Copied files and compiled-in values require redeployment to change, and an unencrypted, unversioned bucket lacks the required controls.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A company with existing Chef cookbooks wants to keep managing server configuration with Chef while using a managed service on AWS. Which service should be used?
options: AWS Elastic Beanstalk with custom scripts
A single large EC2 instance running Chef manually
AWS CodeBuild used as a configuration server
AWS OpsWorks for Chef Automate
items.explanation: OpsWorks for Chef Automate is a managed Chef server that runs existing cookbooks. Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications rather than running a Chef server, a self-managed instance is not highly available or managed, and CodeBuild is a build service, not a configuration management server.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A team wants to eliminate configuration drift by replacing running instances with new ones built from a tested image on every change instead of modifying servers in place. Which practice does this describe?
options: Immutable infrastructure using golden AMIs
In-place patching of long-lived servers
Manual configuration changes recorded in a wiki
Mutable servers updated by a nightly script
items.explanation: Immutable infrastructure replaces instances with freshly built, tested images on each change, which removes drift and makes rollback reliable. In-place patching, manual changes, and nightly scripts leave accumulated divergence on long-lived servers.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.domain: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code
items.stem: A team configures an Elastic Beanstalk environment and needs to install a monitoring agent and set an environment variable on every instance in a repeatable way. Where should these customizations be defined?
options: In an email sent to the operations team
In .ebextensions configuration files committed with the application
By logging into each instance after it launches
In a screenshot of the console settings
items.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk applies .ebextensions configuration files during environment creation and updates, so customizations are repeatable and versioned. Manual logins, screenshots, and emails are not automated and do not persist through scaling or rebuilds.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code

items.stem: A production database must remain available if a single Availability Zone fails and must fail over without application changes to the connection endpoint. Which Amazon RDS configuration should be used?
options: A larger instance class in the same Availability Zone
A single-AZ instance with nightly snapshots
A Multi-AZ deployment with a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone
A read replica in the same Availability Zone
items.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in a different Availability Zone and fails over automatically by repointing the instance endpoint. Single-AZ snapshots require a manual restore, a same-AZ replica shares the failure domain, and a larger instance does not add redundancy.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A web tier behind an Elastic Load Balancer must automatically replace instances that fail application health checks and maintain capacity under demand. Which configuration provides this self-healing behavior?
options: A fixed set of instances with no Auto Scaling group
An Auto Scaling group that checks only EC2 status
Instances that operators restart after receiving email alerts
An Auto Scaling group with ELB health checks enabled and a minimum capacity
items.explanation: An Auto Scaling group using ELB health checks replaces instances that fail application-level checks and maintains minimum capacity while scaling. A fixed fleet cannot self-heal, EC2-only checks miss application failures, and manual restarts are slow and error-prone.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A company wants traffic to move automatically to a standby Region when the primary Region becomes unavailable to users. Which Route 53 configuration should be used?
options: Failover routing with health checks on both Regions
A single record with a very long time to live
Weighted records with equal weights and no health checks
A record that points only to the primary Region
items.explanation: Failover routing with health checks directs users to the secondary endpoint when the primary fails its check. A single record or a primary-only record cannot redirect, and equal weights without health checks keep sending traffic to the failed Region.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A company needs a disaster recovery strategy with the lowest cost that can tolerate a recovery time of many hours while keeping backups in a separate Region. Which strategy fits?
options: Warm standby with a scaled-down running copy
Backup and restore to a separate Region
Pilot light with a continuously replicated database
Multi-site active-active in two Regions
items.explanation: Backup and restore keeps only periodic backups, giving the lowest cost but the longest recovery time, which matches the stated tolerance. Multi-site, warm standby, and pilot light keep running infrastructure, so they recover faster but cost more.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A microservice calls a dependency that is intermittently slow, causing request threads to pile up and failures to cascade. Which pattern should be applied so calls fail fast and recovery is detected automatically?
options: Unlimited growth of the thread pool
Removal of all timeouts so calls can finish
A circuit breaker that opens after a failure threshold and probes for recovery
Immediate retries in an infinite loop
items.explanation: A circuit breaker trips after repeated failures, fails fast instead of piling up threads, and periodically probes for recovery. Infinite immediate retries worsen the overload, an unbounded thread pool hides the problem and exhausts memory, and removing timeouts lets slow calls block even longer.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: An application is throttled by a downstream API during traffic spikes and must retry without amplifying the load on the dependency. Which retry strategy should be used?
options: A single fixed retry after one second regardless of load
No retries at all
Immediate retries as fast as the client can issue them
Exponential backoff with jitter between attempts
items.explanation: Exponential backoff with jitter spaces retries out and randomizes them so many clients do not retry at the same instant, which avoids a retry storm. Immediate retries amplify throttling, a fixed delay can synchronize clients, and disabling retries leaves transient errors unrecovered.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A system must not lose messages that an application cannot process, and operators need to inspect and replay them later. Which design provides this?
options: Configure a dead-letter queue for messages that exceed the receive count
Increase the visibility timeout indefinitely
Disable the queue and process messages inline
Delete the message immediately when any error occurs
items.explanation: A dead-letter queue captures messages that repeatedly fail processing so they can be examined and redelivered without loss. Deleting failed messages loses data, an endless visibility timeout hides poisoning messages, and processing inline removes the durability of the queue.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A company needs a relational database that can survive the loss of an entire Region and allow a secondary Region to be promoted quickly. Which service feature should be used?
options: A larger primary instance class
Amazon Aurora Global Database with a secondary Region cluster
A read replica in the same Region
Nightly snapshots copied to an S3 bucket
items.explanation: Aurora Global Database maintains replicas in another Region and can promote a secondary Region quickly, providing cross-Region disaster recovery. A same-Region replica does not survive a Regional failure, snapshot copies require slow restores, and a larger instance adds no Regional redundancy.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: An Auto Scaling group must drain connections and finish in-flight work before terminating an instance during scale-in. Which feature should be configured?
options: A larger minimum capacity that prevents scale-in
A load balancer configured with sticky sessions
An Auto Scaling life cycle hook that delays termination so the instance can drain
A shorter health check grace period
items.explanation: A terminating life cycle hook pauses instance termination so the application can drain and complete work before the instance goes away. Shortening the grace period terminates faster, blocking scale-in wastes capacity, and sticky sessions do not coordinate graceful shutdown.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A web application stores session state in individual instance memory, so scaling and instance replacement log users out. Which change makes the tier resilient?
options: Increase the instance size to hold more sessions
Keep sessions only in browser cookies with no server state
Enable sticky sessions and never replace instances
Externalize session state to a shared data store such as ElastiCache
items.explanation: Moving session state to a shared store lets any instance serve any user and allows instances to be replaced freely. Sticky sessions still lose state when an instance fails, a larger instance does not share state, and dropping server-side state is not always feasible.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: A company wants to prove that its failover automation actually works before a real outage occurs. Which activity builds the most confidence?
options: Running controlled game days that inject failures and observe recovery
Assuming Multi-AZ guarantees recovery and skipping drills
Writing a runbook that is never exercised
Reviewing the design document once a year
items.explanation: Game days exercise the failover path under controlled conditions and expose gaps in automation and runbooks. Design reviews and assumptions do not test behavior, and an unexercised runbook may be stale when it is needed.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Resilient Cloud Solutions

items.stem: An application must publish business metrics such as orders per minute to CloudWatch so the team can graph and alarm on them. Which action should the application take?
options: Rely on the default EC2 metrics to reflect orders
Call the CloudWatch PutMetricData API with a custom namespace
Write the metric value into a CloudTrail trail
Store the metric in an S3 object and read it manually
items.explanation: Applications publish custom metrics with PutMetricData under their own namespace so CloudWatch can graph and alarm on them. CloudTrail records API activity, S3 objects do not feed metric alarms, and default EC2 metrics do not capture business events.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A team wants a CloudWatch alarm to fire when the word ERROR appears in application log events. Which feature should be used?
options: A CloudTrail trail that scans log text
An S3 lifecycle rule applied to the log bucket
A metric filter on the log group that counts the pattern, with an alarm on the resulting metric
A manual daily review of the log files
items.explanation: Metric filters turn log patterns into CloudWatch metrics, which can then drive an alarm. Manual reviews are not timely, CloudTrail records API calls rather than scanning log text, and lifecycle rules only manage object retention.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A company wants logs from many accounts and services aggregated into a central account for analysis and retention. Which design centralizes log collection?
options: Reading each account logs from the console when needed
Deleting logs locally after one week
Emailing log files to the operations group
CloudWatch Logs subscription filters that stream to a central destination such as Kinesis Data Firehose and S3
items.explanation: Subscription filters stream log events in near real time to a central destination and storage, giving one place to analyze and retain logs. Console reading does not scale, deleting logs loses history, and email is not a durable centralized store.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: An operator must find the slowest requests in a large CloudWatch log group without exporting the logs elsewhere. Which tool should be used?
options: CloudWatch Logs Insights queries against the log group
Downloading every log file to a laptop
A CloudTrail lookup of management events
An AWS Config rule on the log group
items.explanation: Logs Insights runs interactive queries over log data in place to filter and aggregate fields such as request duration. Downloading logs to a laptop is slow and insecure, CloudTrail records API events, and Config rules evaluate resource configuration.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A distributed application needs end-to-end tracing to find which service adds latency to a request. Which service should be enabled?
options: AWS Config recording resource changes
AWS X-Ray with the SDK or daemon instrumenting the services
AWS CloudTrail with data events on S3
Amazon Inspector scanning the instances
items.explanation: X-Ray instruments requests across services to produce a trace and service map that shows where time is spent. CloudTrail records API calls, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Config records configuration changes, none of which trace request paths.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A security team needs a tamper-evident record of AWS API calls and must be able to prove that delivered log files were not altered afterward. Which CloudTrail feature should be enabled?
options: An S3 lifecycle policy that expires the logs
A VPC flow log on each subnet
Log file validation that produces a digest file
A CloudWatch dashboard of API call counts
items.explanation: CloudTrail log file validation creates a digest that can verify delivered log files were not modified, supporting tamper evidence. A dashboard only visualizes counts, a lifecycle policy deletes logs, and flow logs capture network traffic rather than API activity.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A company wants to control the cost of CloudWatch Logs by automatically removing old log events that are no longer needed. Which setting should be applied to each log group?
options: A metric filter that counts log events
A subscription filter that sends events to Lambda
A larger log group size limit
A retention period on the log group
items.explanation: Setting a retention period on a log group expires old events automatically so storage cost stays bounded. Metric and subscription filters process events but do not remove them, and increasing size limits raises rather than lowers exposure.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A team wants to be alerted only when both CPU is high and the request queue is deep, which reduces noise from single-condition alarms. Which CloudWatch feature should be used?
options: A composite alarm that combines the two underlying alarms
Two independent alarms that each page separately
A single alarm on CPU utilization only
A dashboard with no alarms configured
items.explanation: A composite alarm fires only when its referenced alarms are in the required states, which reduces noise from single conditions. Separate alarms page on either condition, a single CPU alarm ignores the queue, and a dashboard does not notify anyone.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A company wants CloudWatch to detect unusual metric behavior without manually setting a static threshold for every time of day. Which feature should be used?
options: A composite alarm with no member alarms
Anomaly detection bands on the metric
A static threshold set to the all-time maximum
A metric filter on the log group
items.explanation: Anomaly detection learns the normal pattern of a metric and alarms when values fall outside the expected band, adapting to daily cycles. A maximum threshold is static and misses new patterns, metric filters work on logs, and a composite alarm needs member alarms.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: CloudWatch by default cannot report memory and disk usage for EC2 instances. Which action makes those operating-system metrics available?
options: Enable VPC flow logs for the instances
Attach an IAM role to the instances
Install and configure the CloudWatch agent on the instances
Enable detailed monitoring in the EC2 console
items.explanation: The CloudWatch agent collects operating-system metrics such as memory and disk that are not available from the hypervisor. Detailed monitoring only raises the resolution of default metrics, flow logs capture network data, and an IAM role grants permissions but collects nothing by itself.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A Lambda function must emit custom metrics efficiently without making a separate CloudWatch API call for every data point. Which approach should be used?
options: Call PutMetricData once per request inside a tight loop
Store the metrics in the function local file system
Print the metrics to standard output without structure
Write metrics as structured JSON to CloudWatch Logs using the embedded metric format
items.explanation: The embedded metric format lets a function emit metrics through its logs asynchronously, avoiding a per-metric API call. Looping PutMetricData is slow and costly, the local file system is ephemeral, and unstructured output cannot be turned into metrics.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Monitoring and Logging

items.stem: A company wants an automated notification or action whenever a specific CloudWatch alarm changes state. Which service should route the event?
options: An Amazon EventBridge rule that matches the alarm state-change event
A CloudTrail trail that filters the alarm
An S3 event notification on the alarm
A Route 53 health check
items.explanation: EventBridge can match CloudWatch alarm state-change events and route them to targets such as Lambda, SNS, or Systems Manager. CloudTrail records the API call but does not route events, S3 notifications apply to bucket objects, and health checks monitor endpoints.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A security team wants an AWS Config rule to correct a non-compliant resource automatically without any human action. Which feature should be configured on the rule?
options: A CloudTrail trail created for the resource
An automatic remediation action that runs an Systems Manager Automation document
A manual remediation note attached to the rule
An SNS topic that delivers weekly compliance reports
items.explanation: AWS Config supports automatic remediation that runs a Systems Manager Automation document when a resource is non-compliant, correcting it without human intervention. Notes, reports, and trails do not change the resource.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A company wants an EC2 instance quarantined automatically when GuardDuty reports that it is communicating with a known malicious host. Which flow should be implemented?
options: Store the finding in S3 and review it next quarter
Disable GuardDuty to reduce the volume of alerts
Route the GuardDuty finding through EventBridge to a Lambda function that applies a quarantine security group
Email the finding to the security team for manual handling
items.explanation: GuardDuty findings are delivered as events that EventBridge can match to invoke a Lambda function which isolates the instance, achieving automatic containment. Email and periodic review are slow, and disabling detection removes protection.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A company wants a repeatable, auditable runbook that performs a multi-step remediation such as stopping an instance and detaching a role. Which Systems Manager capability should be used?
options: A wiki page that lists the manual steps
A CloudWatch dashboard showing the affected resources
An S3 bucket of scripts that a person runs by hand
An Automation document that runs the remediation steps
items.explanation: Systems Manager Automation documents define and execute multi-step remediation as a repeatable, auditable workflow. A wiki and manual scripts are not automated or auditable, and a dashboard only displays data.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: An application tier must add capacity automatically when the average CPU utilization stays above a threshold. Which mechanism should be used?
options: A target tracking scaling policy on the Auto Scaling group
A CloudWatch alarm that only sends email to the team
A manual decision to launch more instances
An S3 lifecycle rule applied to the data bucket
items.explanation: A target tracking policy adjusts capacity to hold a metric such as average CPU near a target, reacting automatically to load. An email alarm does not act, manual launches are slow, and lifecycle rules apply to storage objects.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A company wants an S3 bucket that is accidentally made public to be remediated automatically. Which combination should be used?
options: A weekly manual audit of all bucket policies
An AWS Config rule for public read access with automatic remediation that removes the public policy
A billing alarm that fires when data transfer increases
A CloudTrail trail enabled for the bucket
items.explanation: A Config rule can detect public access and trigger automatic remediation that removes the exposing policy, restoring compliance quickly. Billing alarms and trails only report, and weekly audits leave the bucket exposed for days.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A company wants to respond to AWS service health events, such as a scheduled maintenance notification, with an automated workflow. Which service delivers these events to a target?
options: An S3 inventory report
A VPC flow log
Amazon EventBridge with rules that match AWS Health events
Amazon Macie findings
items.explanation: EventBridge can match AWS Health events and route them to automation so scheduled maintenance or outages trigger a response. Macie classifies data, inventory lists objects, and flow logs capture network traffic.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A deployment must revert automatically if a CloudWatch alarm fires during the rollout. Which combination achieves automated rollback?
options: A pipeline stage where an operator notices the alarm and rolls back by hand
A dashboard that the team watches during releases
A larger deployment timeout
A CodeDeploy deployment group associated with the alarm and automatic rollback enabled
items.explanation: Associating the alarm with the deployment group and enabling automatic rollback makes CodeDeploy revert to the last good revision when the alarm fires. Waiting for an operator is slow, a dashboard does not act, and a longer timeout does not correct a bad release.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A central operations account must receive events from workload accounts so it can run shared remediation. Which EventBridge capability supports this?
options: Cross-account event buses with rules in the central account receiving events from member accounts
Copying the same Lambda function into every account
A single trail enabled in one account only
A shared IAM user used by every account
items.explanation: EventBridge supports cross-account event delivery through event buses so a central account can run shared remediation. Copying functions duplicates maintenance, a single trail records one account, and a shared IAM user violates least privilege.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: A company wants operators to track and resolve security incidents as tickets with diagnostic context attached, created automatically from findings. Which Systems Manager capability should be used?
options: An S3 bucket of incident screenshots
OpsCenter, which creates OpsItems that aggregate context and track resolution
A spreadsheet of incidents kept by the team
A CloudWatch dashboard showing incident counts
items.explanation: OpsCenter creates OpsItems that aggregate diagnostic context and let operators track incidents to resolution, and items can be created automatically from events. Spreadsheets, dashboards, and screenshots do not provide structured incident tracking.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Incident and Event Response

items.stem: An application in one account must encrypt and decrypt data with a customer managed key in a central security account. Which mechanism grants the application least-privilege access without editing the key policy for every caller?
options: Making the key policy allow the account root of every account
Embedding the key material in the application configuration
A KMS grant issued to the application role for the required encrypt and decrypt operations
Exporting the key material to the application account as plaintext
items.explanation: KMS grants delegate specific operations to named principals and can be created and revoked without changing the key policy, supporting least privilege. Symmetric key material cannot be exported as plaintext, a wildcard principal is too broad, and embedding key material is insecure.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company stores a database password in AWS Secrets Manager and wants it rotated on a schedule without changing the application code. Which configuration should be used?
options: Store the password in a comment inside the application source
Place the password in an S3 object with public read access
Keep the password static and rotate it manually once a year
Enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function and a rotation schedule
items.explanation: Secrets Manager can rotate a secret automatically with a Lambda rotation function on a schedule, and the application retrieves the current value from the service. Hard-coded or public secrets are exposed, and manual annual rotation is slow and error-prone.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A CodeBuild project needs permissions to deploy resources, and the security team requires least privilege. How should permissions be granted?
options: Attach a scoped IAM role to the project that allows only the required actions
Store long-lived IAM user access keys in the buildspec
Give the project administrator access for simplicity
Use the account root credentials inside the build
items.explanation: A scoped service role grants CodeBuild only the actions it needs, which follows least privilege. Long-lived keys in the buildspec are exposed, administrator access is excessive, and root credentials must never be used.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company wants to cap the maximum permissions an application role can ever have, regardless of the identity policies later attached to it. Which mechanism should be used?
options: A resource tag placed on the role
An IAM permissions boundary attached to the role
An S3 bucket policy scoped to the role
A CloudWatch alarm on the role API calls
items.explanation: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions for an entity so that even broader identity policies cannot exceed the boundary. A bucket policy governs one resource, an alarm only monitors, and a tag carries metadata.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company must prevent member account administrators from disabling CloudTrail in their own accounts. Which control should be applied at the organization level?
options: A CloudWatch alarm on CloudTrail API calls
A statement in the security policy document
A service control policy that denies the CloudTrail stop and delete actions
An IAM policy in each account that allows only CloudTrail actions
items.explanation: A service control policy at the organization level caps permissions for all principals, including account administrators, so it can deny turning off CloudTrail. An allow-only IAM policy can be changed by the administrator, an alarm only notices, and documentation does not enforce.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company wants continuous detection of threats such as compromised credentials and cryptocurrency mining across all of its AWS accounts. Which service should be enabled with organization-wide administration?
options: AWS CloudTrail operating alone
Amazon Macie
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
items.explanation: GuardDuty continuously analyzes account, network, and DNS activity to detect threats and supports delegated administration across an organization. CloudTrail records activity but does not analyze it, Macie classifies S3 data, and Config evaluates resource configuration.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company wants container image vulnerabilities identified during the build pipeline so that unsafe images never reach production. Which service should be integrated with the pipeline?
options: Amazon Inspector scanning the images, with the pipeline failing on findings above a threshold
AWS Trusted Advisor best-practice checks
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS CloudTrail
items.explanation: Inspector scans container images for vulnerabilities, and the pipeline can fail a stage when findings exceed a threshold. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, while GuardDuty and CloudTrail detect or record activity rather than scan images.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company must continuously assess its resources against an industry framework and package the controls for deployment to many accounts. Which AWS Config feature should be used?
options: An S3 inventory report
A conformance pack that bundles Config rules for deployment
A single Config rule created by hand in one account
A CloudTrail trail forwarded to S3
items.explanation: Conformance packs package a collection of Config rules and remediation actions that can be deployed together across accounts to assess a framework. A single hand-made rule does not scale, trails record activity, and inventory lists objects.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company collects findings from multiple AWS security services and wants one normalized view across its organization. Which service should be used?
options: AWS Artifact
Amazon Inspector
AWS Security Hub with organization-wide aggregation
Amazon CloudWatch Logs alone
items.explanation: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings from AWS services and partner tools into a single view and supports organization aggregation. CloudWatch Logs stores raw logs, Artifact provides compliance reports, and Inspector scans specific resource types.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company must ensure that an S3 bucket used for logs can never be made public, even by mistake. Which control should be applied?
options: Rely on the bucket name being difficult to guess
Grant read access to all authenticated AWS users
Remove server-side encryption from the bucket
Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket and at the account level
items.explanation: S3 Block Public Access prevents public policies and ACLs from exposing the bucket and can be enforced at the account level. An obscure name is not a control, authenticated-user read still exposes data, and removing encryption weakens protection.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company wants the artifacts stored by CodePipeline to be encrypted with a key that the company controls. Which configuration should be used?
options: Configure the pipeline artifact store to use a customer managed KMS key
Store the artifacts in an unencrypted S3 bucket
Email the artifacts to the team instead of storing them
Encrypt the artifacts with an SSH key pair
items.explanation: CodePipeline artifact stores use S3 and can be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key so the company controls access and rotation. An unencrypted bucket exposes artifacts, email is not a store, and an SSH key is not a data-encryption mechanism.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A security team wants to identify resources shared with external principals and uncover unintended public access grants. Which service should be used?
options: AWS Shield Advanced
IAM Access Analyzer
AWS CloudTrail Insights
Amazon GuardDuty
items.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes resource policies and role trust policies to flag resources reachable by external principals. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API patterns, GuardDuty detects threats, and Shield protects against DDoS.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance

items.stem: A company terminates TLS for a public site on an Application Load Balancer and wants managed certificates that renew automatically for the domain. Which service should be used?
options: An SSH key pair generated in EC2
AWS CloudHSM alone storing the private key
AWS Certificate Manager with a certificate attached to the load balancer
A self-signed certificate copied to every instance
items.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager issues public TLS certificates for integrated services and renews them automatically, removing manual certificate maintenance. Self-signed certificates cause trust warnings and expire manually, SSH keys are for host access, and CloudHSM stores keys but does not issue or renew certificates.
items.reference: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 Exam Guide - Security and Compliance
